mainTopic: Which ברכה to make on processed or unusual foods (oil, flour, heart of palm), and the caper-bush under ערלה outside ארץ ישראל
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous amud's discussion of oil drunk in אניגרון, a vegetable broth. The גמרא asks why the oil is not just a side ingredient (טפל) to the broth. It answers that the case is a person with a sore throat, for whom the oil is the main thing, and that he makes a ברכה because he enjoys it even though it is medicine. Next, רב יהודה and רב נחמן argue whether plain wheat flour gets בורא פרי האדמה or שהכל. The גמרא concludes that both wheat and barley flour get שהכל, and that even harmful barley flour needs a ברכה because a person enjoys it. Then רב יהודה and שמואל argue about קורא (heart of palm). The הלכה follows שמואל that it gets שהכל, because nobody plants a palm tree for its קורא. Finally, the גמרא discusses רב's ruling that for an ערלה caper-bush outside ארץ ישראל one throws away the berries but eats the buds, following the lenient view of רבי עקיבא. רבינא challenges מר בר רב אשי for not following בית שמאי, who are even more lenient, and that argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the definition of the vegetable broths
steps.stepSummary: The tail of a definition: one of the broths is made from all kinds of boiled vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: …of all boiled vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence on the previous amud. That sentence defined the broths mentioned in the discussion, and this one is the broth made from all boiled vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said אניגרון is beet water and אכסיגרון is the water of all boiled vegetables. These words close that second definition. The point to hold onto is that oil was being drunk mixed into a vegetable broth, and the next steps build on that.

keyTerms.meaning: A broth made from boiled vegetable water, mixed with oil

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the end of a sentence that began on the previous page, so do not try to read it on its own.

phrases.english: of all boiled vegetables.
phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier line: אכסיגרון is the water of all boiled vegetables.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלְּהוּ שִׁלְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a definition begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The broths into which the oil is mixed are vegetable waters.

steps.title: Challenge: the broth should be the main food, not the oil
steps.stepSummary: If the oil is drunk inside אניגרון, the broth is the main food, so by the rule of עיקר וטפל the ברכה should go on the broth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then the אניגרון is the main food and the oil is secondary. And we learned in a משנה: This is the rule. Whenever there is a main food together with a secondary food, you make the ברכה on the main food, and that ברכה covers the secondary food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that oil gets בורא פרי העץ when it is drunk in אניגרון. It argues the oil there is only a side ingredient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a famous rule in a משנה: a secondary food is covered by the ברכה on the main food. Normally oil is added to a broth only for flavor, so the oil should be טפל. That means the ברכה should go on the אניגרון, not the oil's בורא פרי העץ.

keyTerms.meaning: And we learned in a משנה
Exempts; covers so no separate ברכה is needed

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of עיקר וטפל is a basic principle in the laws of ברכות. It decides which ברכה you make whenever foods are mixed or eaten together.

phrases.english: If so, it would be that
the anigeron is primary and the oil is secondary,
and we learned in a mishna: This is the principle:
Anything that is primary and has a secondary food with it,
one makes the blessing on the primary food
and thereby exempts the secondary food!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵה לֵיהּ אֲנִיגְרוֹן עִיקָּר וְשֶׁמֶן טָפֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the earlier claim that oil drunk with אניגרון gets בורא פרי העץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one makes בורא פרי העץ on oil drunk with אניגרון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a mix of broth and oil, the broth is the main food. By the משנה's rule of עיקר וטפל, the oil should be covered by the broth's ברכה.

steps.title: Answer: the case is a person with a sore throat
steps.stepSummary: The case is someone drinking the oil to heal a sore throat, so the oil is the main thing he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Someone who has a sore throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case to a person with a sore throat. That makes the oil, not the broth, the main ingredient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Main versus secondary depends on what the person is after. Someone soothing a sore throat wants the oil, and the אניגרון just helps it go down. So here the oil is עיקר and gets its own ברכה of בורא פרי העץ.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (Narrows the case to answer a question)
One who has a sore throat

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not reject the rule of עיקר וטפל. It keeps the rule and shows that in this case the oil is the עיקר.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's usual way of saying the case here is a narrower one.

phrases.english: With one who has a sore throat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil mixed into broth is always just a side ingredient.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the oil is taken to soothe a sore throat, the oil is the main ingredient and gets בורא פרי העץ.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows people drink oil in broth for sore throats
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about שבת shows that putting a lot of oil into אניגרון and swallowing it is a known way to treat a sore throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Someone with a sore throat should not gargle with oil on שבת in the first place. But he may put a lot of oil into אניגרון and swallow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the case it just described really happens. People drink lots of oil in אניגרון to treat a sore throat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת there is a rabbinic decree against obvious healing, so gargling oil is not allowed. Swallowing oil in broth looks like normal eating, so it is allowed. The ברייתא shows that 'a lot of oil' is the healing ingredient here, which is why the oil counts as עיקר.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is also a source for the laws of healing on שבת. Something that looks like ordinary eating or drinking is allowed even if the person intends it for healing.

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who has a sore throat
should not gargle it with oil in the first place on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Gargling is clearly medical, so it is forbidden because of the decree against healing on שבת.

phrases.english: but he may put a large amount of oil
into the anigeron and swallow it.
phrases.notes: This looks like normal eating, so it is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַחוֹשֵׁשׁ בִּגְרוֹנוֹ לֹא יְעָרְעֶנּוּ בְּשֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the case described in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That drinking a lot of oil in אניגרון for a sore throat is a real, known practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about treating a sore throat on שבת.

steps.title: Challenge: isn't it obvious he makes a ברכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need to be told this person makes a ברכה. That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges whether the ruling teaches anything new. Since he is drinking the oil, of course he should make a ברכה. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the oil is the main ingredient and he is drinking it, a ברכה seems automatic. The גמרא assumes every teaching should add something new, so it asks what this one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (Asks why a ruling needs to be stated)

phrases.english: This is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the ruling, now explained, teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to state that the sore-throat drinker makes a ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Drinking oil as the main ingredient obviously needs a ברכה, so the teaching seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Answer: medicine still needs a ברכה if you enjoy it
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought healing intent cancels the ברכה. The teaching shows that because he enjoys it, he must make a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since he means it as medicine, he should not make a ברכה on it at all. So it teaches us: since he gets enjoyment from it, he must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what is new in the ruling. Healing intent does not remove the ברכה when the person enjoys what he drinks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea (הוה אמינא) was that medicine is not food, so it needs no ברכה. The conclusion is that a ברכה is tied to the הנאה, the enjoyment. If he enjoys the taste, he blesses, whatever his reason for drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: Oil drunk in אניגרון gets בורא פרי העץ only when the oil is the main thing, such as for a sore throat. Even when a person eats or drinks for healing, he makes a ברכה if he enjoys it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the halachic principle that the ברכה depends on enjoyment. Food or drink taken for health still needs a ברכה when it tastes good.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
since he intends it for healing,
he should not make a blessing on it at all,
it teaches us
that since he has enjoyment from it,
he needs to make a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלִרְפוּאָה קָא מְכַוֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing what is new (מהו דתימא, קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he drinks for healing, it counts as medicine and needs no ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since he enjoys it, he must make a ברכה even though he drinks it for healing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברכה follows the enjoyment, not the reason for eating.

steps.title: Dispute over the blessing on wheat flour
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says plain wheat flour gets בורא פרי האדמה. רב נחמן says it gets שהכל נהיה בדברו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wheat flour: רב יהודה said its ברכה is 'בורא פרי האדמה', and רב נחמן said it is 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question: what ברכה do you make if you eat plain wheat flour? Two אמוראים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grinding wheat into flour changes the grain. רב יהודה holds that flour still counts as the produce of the ground, so it keeps בורא פרי האדמה. רב נחמן holds that flour has changed too much, or is not a normal way to eat wheat, so it only gets the general ברכה of שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה on produce that grows from the ground
The general ברכה: 'by Whose word all things came to be'

phrases.english: Wheat flour:
Rav Yehuda said: 'Who creates fruit of the ground,'
and Rav Nachman said: 'By Whose word all things came to be.'

steps.triggerLanguage: קִמְחָא דְחִיטֵּי, רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the discussion of oil drunk for a sore throat. The link is that both topics deal with foods that have been processed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה: wheat flour gets בורא פרי האדמה. רב נחמן: wheat flour gets שהכל.

steps.title: רבא supports רב יהודה from the ברכה on olive oil
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב נחמן not to argue with רב יהודה. Both רבי יוחנן and שמואל rule that olive oil gets בורא פרי העץ. So a food that has changed form keeps its original ברכה, and flour should keep בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Don't argue with רב יהודה, because רבי יוחנן and שמואל hold like him. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, and רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: on olive oil we say 'בורא פרי העץ'. This shows that even though the olive changed, it keeps its ברכה. Here too, even though the wheat changed, it keeps its ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a proof for רב יהודה from a ruling about olive oil. He uses it to tell רב נחמן to stop disagreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Olive oil is a changed form of the olive, yet it still gets בורא פרי העץ, the same ברכה as the fruit itself. רבא applies the same logic to flour: it is a changed form of wheat, so it should keep בורא פרי האדמה. The proof is especially strong because two major authorities, רבי יוחנן and שמואל, stand behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: It stays in its original status

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Do not disagree with Rav Yehuda,
because Rabbi Yochanan and Shmuel hold like him.
As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and so too Rabbi Yitzchak said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן זַיִת מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָעֵץ״.
phrases.english: Over olive oil, one says 'Who creates fruit of the tree.'

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִשְׁתַּנִּי — בְּמִלְּתֵיהּ קָאֵי.
phrases.english: This shows: even though it changed, it keeps its original status.
phrases.notes: The olive turned into oil, yet it keeps the fruit's ברכה.

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִשְׁתַּנִּי — בְּמִלְּתֵיהּ קָאֵי.
phrases.english: Here too, even though it changed, it keeps its original status.
phrases.notes: The wheat turned into flour, so it should keep בורא פרי האדמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: לָא תִּפְלוֹג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's side of the dispute in step 7 and pushes back on רב נחמן.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that wheat flour gets בורא פרי האדמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי יוחנן and שמואל that olive oil gets בורא פרי העץ, showing that a changed food keeps its original ברכה

steps.title: Olive oil and flour are not comparable
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Olive oil is the finished product and cannot be improved further. Flour can still be improved by baking it into bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it the same? There, the oil has no further improvement. Here, the flour has a further improvement: bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. It shows that oil and flour are different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil is the final, best use of the olive, so it makes sense for it to carry the fruit's ברכה. Flour is only a middle stage on the way to bread, its real final form. So raw flour may not deserve בורא פרי האדמה, and רב נחמן's view of שהכל can stand.

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There, it has no further improvement,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא — אִית לֵיהּ עִלּוּיָא אַחֲרִינָא בְּפַת.
phrases.english: here, it has a further improvement, as bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם לֵית לֵיהּ עִלּוּיָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison between olive oil and flour that רבא used in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from olive oil. It does not show that רב יהודה is wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Oil is a finished product with no further improvement. Flour can still become bread, so the two cases are different.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea of עלויא אחרינא. If a food can still be improved into something better, its in-between form may lose its special ברכה.

steps.title: Challenge from שמואל's ruling on barley flour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a food with further potential gets only שהכל. שמואל said raw gourd and barley flour get שהכל. That implies wheat flour gets בורא פרי האדמה, even though wheat flour can also become bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it true that when something can still be improved, we don't say 'בורא פרי האדמה' on it, only 'שהכל'? But רבי זירא said in the name of רב מתנא, who said in the name of שמואל: on raw gourd and on barley flour we say 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'. Doesn't that mean that on wheat flour we say 'בורא פרי האדמה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 9 using a teaching of שמואל. It reads that teaching closely to make an inference about wheat flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל names only barley flour as getting שהכל. The implication is that wheat flour is different and gets בורא פרי האדמה. Yet wheat flour can still be made into bread, so the rule of עלויא אחרינא from step 9 seems wrong, and רב יהודה's view looks correct again.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (opens a contradiction)
Doesn't it mean that...? (draws an inference)

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל never directly says anything about wheat flour. The challenge comes from what he left out: by naming only barley flour, he implies that wheat flour is different.

phrases.english: And when it has a further improvement,
do we not say over it 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
but only 'By Whose word all things'?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Zeira say in the name of Rav Mattana, in the name of Shmuel:
Over raw gourd and barley flour
we say over them 'By Whose word all things came to be.'

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו דְּחִיטֵּי בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה!
phrases.english: Doesn't that mean that over wheat flour one says 'Who creates fruit of the ground'!
phrases.notes: Barley flour is not normally eaten raw, but wheat flour apparently gets the higher ברכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אִית לֵיהּ עִלּוּיָא אַחֲרִינָא לָא מְבָרְכִינַן עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from step 9 that a food with a further improvement gets only שהכל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 9 that a food with עלויא אחרינא (wheat flour, which can become bread) does not get בורא פרי האדמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules שהכל only on barley flour. That implies wheat flour gets בורא פרי האדמה, even though wheat flour can also become bread. This contradicts the reasoning of step 9.

steps.title: Wheat flour also gets שהכל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from שמואל by saying wheat flour also gets שהכל, not בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Wheat flour also gets the ברכה of 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the inference from step 10. שמואל's ruling on barley flour does not mean that wheat flour gets בורא פרי האדמה, because wheat flour also gets שהכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 tried to infer from שמואל: barley flour gets שהכל, so wheat flour must get something better. The גמרא simply denies that inference. Wheat flour also gets שהכל, so רב נחמן's view stands.

phrases.english: No, over wheat flour also
phrases.notes: This pushes back on the conclusion drawn in step 10.

phrases.english: one says 'By Whose word all things came to be.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּחִיטֵּי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by denying its inference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the inference: the case not mentioned has the same ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל mentioned barley flour, so wheat flour must get a better ברכה (בורא פרי האדמה).
steps.terutzMaskana: Wheat flour also gets שהכל, so שמואל's ruling is no challenge to רב נחמן.

steps.title: Why not mention wheat, which would teach barley automatically?
steps.stepSummary: If wheat flour also gets שהכל, שמואל should have stated it about wheat. Barley would then follow by קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him teach us that wheat flour gets שהכל, and all the more so barley flour!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 11. If both flours get שהכל, mentioning wheat would have taught us both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat is the more important grain. If even wheat flour gets only שהכל, then barley flour certainly does. So naming barley seems to be the weaker, less useful choice.

phrases.english: Then let him teach us about wheat flour,
and all the more so barley flour!
phrases.notes: A קל וחומר: whatever is true of the better grain is certainly true of the lesser one

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַשְׁמְעִינַן דְּחִיטֵּי וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן דִּשְׂעָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11 by asking about שמואל's choice of example.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's choice to mention barley flour instead of wheat flour.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wheat flour also gets שהכל, stating it about wheat would have taught barley by קל וחומר. Naming barley teaches less.

steps.title: Barley had to be mentioned, or we would think it gets no ברכה
steps.stepSummary: Mentioning only wheat might have led us to think barley flour gets no ברכה at all. So שמואל mentions barley to teach that it still gets שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had taught us about wheat, I would have said: this applies only to wheat flour, but over barley flour one makes no ברכה at all. So he teaches us that barley flour also needs a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the קל וחומר does not work automatically. Barley flour might have been thought to need no ברכה whatsoever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was never which ברכה barley flour gets. The question was whether it gets any ברכה. Barley flour is so poor a food that one might think it is not worth a ברכה, so שמואל had to say it gets שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first assumption)
these words apply (only to this case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think barley flour gets a better ברכה than wheat. The worry was the opposite: that barley flour gets no ברכה at all.

phrases.english: If he had taught us about wheat flour,
I would have said: this applies only to wheat flour,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דִּשְׂעָרֵי לָא לְבָרֵיךְ עֲלֵיהּ כְּלָל,
phrases.english: but over barley flour one should not make any ברכה at all,
so he teaches us (that barley flour needs a ברכה).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן דְּחִיטֵּי הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by explaining why barley flour had to be mentioned.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows that the 'obvious' case was needed to block a mistaken assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Barley flour is too poor a food to need any ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Barley flour also gets שהכל, so שמואל had to say so explicitly.

steps.title: Could barley flour be worse than salt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we could think barley flour needs no ברכה, since a משנה says even salt and salt water get שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is barley flour worse than salt and salt water? We learned in a משנה: over salt and over salt water one says 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the הוה אמינא of step 13. If even salt and salt water get a ברכה, surely barley flour does too, so why would שמואל need to say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt and salt water are hardly foods at all, yet they still get שהכל. Barley flour seems at least as good as them. So the mistaken assumption from step 13 seems impossible, and שמואל's statement seems unnecessary again.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: But is it worse than salt and salt water?
As we learned: over salt and over salt water
one says 'By Whose word all things came to be.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי גָּרַע מִמֶּלַח וְזָמִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הוה אמינא assumed in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one might have thought barley flour needs no ברכה at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה gives שהכל even for salt and salt water. Barley flour cannot be worse than them, so it obviously needs a ברכה.

steps.title: Barley flour is harmful, but any enjoyment requires a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: Salt is something people normally put in their mouths, but barley flour is harmful and causes worms, so one might think it needs no ברכה. שמואל teaches that because a person enjoys it, he must make a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: salt and salt water are things people normally put in their mouths. But barley flour, since it is harmful and causes intestinal worms, one should not make a ברכה over it at all. So he teaches us: since he gets enjoyment from it, he must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from step 14. It explains why barley flour really could have seemed worse than salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt is a normal thing to eat, even if only a little. Barley flour is actually harmful to the body, so one might think it does not count as food. The rule is that enjoyment is what matters: if a person enjoys it, he makes a ברכה, even if it is unhealthy.

keyTerms.meaning: it would enter your mind (you might have thought)

steps.whatToRemember: Wheat flour and barley flour both get שהכל. שמואל mentioned barley to teach that even a harmful food needs a ברכה, because a ברכה depends on the enjoyment a person gets.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for the laws of ברכות: the ברכה depends on the enjoyment, not on whether the food is healthy or important.

phrases.english: It was necessary.
It would enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: מֶלַח וְזָמִית עָבֵיד אִינָשׁ דְּשָׁדֵי לְפוּמֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: salt and salt water are things a person normally puts in his mouth,
but barley flour,
since it is harmful and causes intestinal worms,
one should not make any ברכה over it at all.
So he teaches us:
since he gets enjoyment from it,
he must make a ברכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by showing how barley flour differs from salt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: salt is normally eaten, while barley flour is harmful.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because barley flour is harmful, it does not count as food and needs no ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any enjoyment requires a ברכה, so barley flour gets שהכל.

steps.title: Dispute over the blessing on heart of palm
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says קורא gets בורא פרי האדמה. שמואל says it gets שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Heart of palm: רב יהודה said the ברכה is 'Who creates fruit of the ground,' and שמואל said it is 'By Whose word all things came to be.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between רב יהודה and שמואל about which ברכה to make on קורא, the soft inner part of a young palm tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion was about barley flour. This is a new case in the same theme of tricky foods. Only the two rulings are given here, and the reasons come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Heart of palm, the soft edible core at the top of a young palm tree
The ברכה on produce that grows from the ground
The general ברכה for foods that do not get a more specific ברכה

phrases.english: Heart of palm: Rav Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: קורא is the topic heading for this new case.

phrases.english: 'Who creates fruit of the ground,'
and Shmuel said:
'By Whose word all things came to be.'

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹרָא, רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case after the barley-flour discussion ended in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה: בורא פרי האדמה on קורא. שמואל: שהכל.

steps.title: The reasons behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה holds that קורא is a fruit. שמואל holds that it gets שהכל because it will eventually harden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said 'Who creates fruit of the ground' because it is a fruit. שמואל said 'By Whose word all things came to be' because it will eventually harden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why each אמורא ruled the way he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יהודה, what counts is that the food is soft and edible now, so it is like produce. For שמואל, what counts is what it will become. Since קורא turns into hard wood, it is really part of the tree and not a fruit, so it only gets שהכל.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said 'Who creates fruit of the ground,'
because it is a fruit.
And Shmuel said 'By Whose word all things came to be,'
since it will eventually harden.
phrases.notes: It becomes wood, part of the tree itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה״, פֵּירָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the two rulings stated in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute depends on whether we look at the current edible state (fruit) or the final state (hard wood).

steps.title: שמואל praises רב יהודה with a radish argument
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב יהודה that his view makes sense, because a radish also hardens eventually and still gets בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: 'Sharp one, your view makes sense, since a radish eventually hardens, yet we make בורא פרי האדמה on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל himself brings an argument that supports his student רב יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A radish left in the ground also becomes hard and woody. Even so, we make בורא פרי האדמה on a soft radish. This seems to show that 'it will harden later' is not a reason to downgrade the ברכה, which would undercut שמואל's own reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Sharp one,' שמואל's nickname for רב יהודה, praising his sharp mind
It makes sense like your view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not be thrown off that שמואל is arguing for the opposite side. He is acknowledging that his student has a strong point. The גמרא answers this point in the next step.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
Sharp one, it makes sense like your view,
since a radish eventually hardens
and yet we recite over it 'Who creates fruit of the ground.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁינָּנָא, כְּווֹתָךְ מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's side against the 'it will harden' reasoning from step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that קורא gets בורא פרי האדמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted practice of making בורא פרי האדמה on a radish, which also hardens eventually.

steps.title: The גמרא rejects the radish comparison
steps.stepSummary: The radish proof fails, because people plant radishes in order to eat them soft, but nobody plants a palm tree for its קורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. People plant radishes with the soft radish in mind, while people do not plant palm trees with the heart of palm in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the radish argument and defends שמואל's original position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real test is why the plant was grown. A soft radish is the very thing the farmer wants, so it counts as produce. A palm tree is planted for dates, and the קורא is not the purpose of planting, so it does not get the fruit-type ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so, a formula that rejects what was just said
With the intention of, with in mind
Radish, here meaning the soft edible radish

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule for ברכות: a food's ברכה can depend on whether people plant the plant for that part. The next step tests that rule.

phrases.english: But that is not so:
people plant a radish with the soft radish in mind,

phrases.aramaic: דִּקְלָא לָא נָטְעִי אִינָשֵׁי אַדַּעְתָּא דְקוֹרָא.
phrases.english: but people do not plant a palm tree with the heart of palm in mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the radish proof from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the comparison between radish and קורא, which restores שמואל's position.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The radish is planted for its soft edible part, while the palm is not planted for its קורא, so the two cases are different.

steps.title: Challenge from the caper-bush
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'planting intention' rule. Caper-bushes are planted for their buds, yet their leaves and shoots still get בורא פרי האדמה, not שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that whenever people do not plant for that part, we do not make the fruit ברכה on it? What about the caper-bush, which people plant for its buds? We learned in a משנה: on the parts of the caper-bush, the leaves and young shoots get 'Who creates fruit of the ground,' and the berries and buds get 'Who creates fruit of the tree.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from the last step, that a part people do not plant for cannot get a fruit-type ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The caper-bush is planted for its main produce. Its leaves and young shoots are only side parts, yet the משנה gives them בורא פרי האדמה rather than שהכל. So a side part of a plant can still get the ground ברכה, and the same should apply to קורא.

keyTerms.meaning: Its blossoms or buds, the main produce people plant it for
Another name for the caper plant
Caper buds, the outer husk around the berry

phrases.english: And wherever people do not plant
with this in mind, we do not recite that blessing over it?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי צָלָף, דְּנָטְעִי אִינָשֵׁי אַדַּעְתָּא דְפִרְחָא,
phrases.english: But there is the caper-bush, which people plant with its buds in mind,
and we learned in a Mishnah: regarding the parts of the caper plant,
over the leaves and over the young shoots
one says 'Who creates fruit of the ground,'
phrases.notes: These are side parts, yet they get a produce ברכה and not שהכל.

phrases.english: and over the berries and over the buds
one says 'Who creates fruit of the tree.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּלָא נָטְעִי אִינָשֵׁי אַדַּעְתָּא דְּהָכִי לָא מְבָרְכִינַן עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the planting-intention rule used in step 19 to reject the radish proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 19 that a part people do not plant for does not get a fruit-type ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives בורא פרי האדמה to the caper-bush's leaves and shoots, even though people do not plant it for them. So קורא should also get בורא פרי האדמה.

steps.title: Caper-bushes are planted for their shoots, palms are not planted for קורא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the caper-bush challenge. People do plant caper-bushes with the shoots in mind, but nobody plants a palm with the קורא in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: People plant a caper-bush with its shoots in mind. People do not plant a palm tree with its קורא in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 20. The caper-bush does not break the 'planting intention' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 argued that the caper-bush is planted for its fruit, yet its leaves and shoots still get בורא פרי האדמה, which seems to break the planting-intention rule. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that people also plant caper-bushes with the shoots in mind, so it makes sense that the shoots get בורא פרי האדמה. The palm is different: nobody plants it for the קורא, so the rule from Step 19 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: with the intention of / with in mind
the shoots or leaves of the caper-bush

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
a caper-bush, people plant it
with its shoots in mind;
a palm tree, people do not plant it
with the heart of palm in mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: צָלָף נָטְעִי אִינָשֵׁי אַדַּעְתָּא דְשׁוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the caper-bush challenge from Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): the caper's shoots are part of why people plant it, but the palm's קורא is not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Caper shoots get בורא פרי האדמה even though the bush is not planted for them, which would break the planting-intention rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Caper shoots are also part of the planting intention, so the rule holds and קורא still gets שהכל.

steps.title: The הלכה follows שמואל
steps.stepSummary: Even though שמואל praised רב יהודה's view, the final הלכה follows שמואל: קורא gets שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though שמואל praised רב יהודה, the הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling for the קורא debate: the הלכה is like שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18, שמואל praised רב יהודה's position, which might suggest the הלכה follows רב יהודה. The גמרא says no: the praise does not decide the הלכה. The ברכה on קורא is שהכל.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה on קורא (heart of palm) is שהכל, like שמואל. Nobody plants a palm tree for it, so it is not treated as a real food of the tree.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that because שמואל praised רב יהודה's view, the הלכה follows רב יהודה. The גמרא says clearly that the הלכה follows שמואל.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקַלְּסֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: And even though Shmuel praised Rav Yehuda,
the halakha follows Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקַלְּסֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה, הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the קורא debate after the challenge was answered.

steps.title: With an ערלה caper-bush outside ארץ ישראל, throw away the berries but eat the buds
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: for a caper-bush that is ערלה outside ארץ ישראל, one throws away the berries but may eat the buds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: With a caper-bush of ערלה outside ארץ ישראל, one throws away the berries and eats the buds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic linked to the caper-bush. It brings a ruling about ערלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה means fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden. רב says only the berries count as forbidden fruit here, so the buds may be eaten. This suggests that the buds are not considered 'fruit'.

keyTerms.meaning: fruit of a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
caper buds (the outer shell around the fruit)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
a caper-bush of orla outside Eretz Yisrael:
one throws away the berries
and eats the buds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: צָלָף שֶׁל עׇרְלָה בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related ruling about the caper-bush, brought because the caper-bush was just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an ערלה caper-bush outside ארץ ישראל, only the berries are forbidden. The buds are allowed.

steps.title: A משנה treats caper buds as fruit of the tree
steps.stepSummary: Does רב mean that the buds are not fruit? The משנה quoted in step 20 says the buds, like the berries, get בורא פרי העץ, which means they are fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean the berries are fruit and the buds are not? But we learned: On the parts of the caper-bush, on the leaves and young shoots, one says בורא פרי האדמה. On the berries and the buds, one says בורא פרי העץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling. It uses the משנה about ברכות from step 20, which seems to disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling assumes that the buds are not fruit, so ערלה does not apply to them. But the משנה gives the buds the same ברכה as the berries, בורא פרי העץ, which shows they are fruit. If they are fruit, they should be forbidden as ערלה too.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (introduces what the statement seems to imply)
and they pointed out a contradiction

phrases.english: Is that to say that berries are fruit
and buds are not fruit?
And they contrasted it with a source:
Over the parts of the caper-bush:
over the leaves and over the young shoots
one says 'Who creates fruit of the ground';
and over the berries and over the buds
one says 'Who creates fruit of the tree'!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דַּאֲבִיּוֹנוֹת פֵּירֵי וְקַפְרֵיסִין לָאו פֵּירֵי? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רב's ruling implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's implied view that caper buds are not fruit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives the buds בורא פרי העץ, showing they are fruit. So they should be ערלה like the berries.

steps.title: רב follows רבי עקיבא, who says only the berries are fruit
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like רבי עקיבא. In a משנה about מעשר, רבי עקיבא says only the berries are fruit, while רבי אליעזר counts shoots, berries, and buds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב holds like רבי עקיבא. As we learned: רבי אליעזר says a caper-bush is tithed on its shoots, berries, and buds. רבי עקיבא says only the berries are tithed, because only they are fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The משנה about ברכות and רב follow different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an argument between תנאים about which parts of the caper-bush count as fruit. The משנה about ברכות matches the side that counts the buds as fruit. רב follows רבי עקיבא, who counts only the berries, so for רב the buds are not ערלה.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: He ruled in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.
As we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
a caper-bush is tithed
on its young shoots, berries, and buds.
Rabbi Akiva says:
only the berries alone are tithed,
because that is the fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא. דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument between תנאים: רב follows one תנא, and the משנה about ברכות matches the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees caper buds are fruit, so רב's ruling contradicts the משנה about ברכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא holds only the berries are fruit, and רב follows him.

steps.title: Why didn't רב just say the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: If רב follows רבי עקיבא, he should have simply said 'the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him say: 'The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how רב worded his ruling. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא' would have been shorter and clearer. Why did רב instead give a specific case, ערלה outside ארץ ישראל?

phrases.english: Then let him say: 'The halakha follows Rabbi Akiva'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵימָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer that רב follows רבי עקיבא and questions רב's wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simple 'הלכה כרבי עקיבא' would have said the same thing more simply.

steps.title: A lenient view in ערלה applies only outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: If רב had said 'the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא', we would apply it even in ארץ ישראל. His wording teaches that a lenient opinion about ערלה is followed only outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had said 'the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא', I would have thought it applies even in ארץ ישראל. So he teaches us: whoever is lenient in ארץ ישראל, the הלכה follows him outside ארץ ישראל, but not in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב worded his ruling as a specific case: to limit it to outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה outside ארץ ישראל is less strict, so we may follow a lenient opinion there. In ארץ ישראל we do not follow the lenient view, so the buds stay forbidden. By naming 'outside ארץ ישראל', רב teaches this limit.
steps.whatToRemember: In ערלה, a lenient opinion is followed outside ארץ ישראל but not inside it. That is why רב allowed the caper buds only outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a general rule for ערלה: outside ארץ ישראל we may rely on a lenient view.

phrases.english: If he had said 'the halakha follows Rabbi Akiva',
I would have thought: even in Eretz Yisrael.
So he teaches us:
anyone who is lenient regarding Eretz Yisrael,
the halakha follows him outside Eretz Yisrael,
but in Eretz Yisrael, not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא אֲפִילּוּ בָּאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question from Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording: the specific case limits the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A general 'הלכה כרבי עקיבא' would allow the buds even in ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: A lenient view in ערלה is followed only outside ארץ ישראל, so the buds are allowed only there.

steps.title: Why not use the general rule about lenient opinions outside the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רב could have said 'the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא outside ארץ ישראל', based on the known rule that anyone who is lenient in the land is followed outside the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let רב say: 'The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא outside ארץ ישראל', since the rule is that whoever is lenient about the land, the הלכה follows him outside the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 27. It suggests a cleaner way רב could have said his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said רב used his special wording to teach that we follow a lenient view only outside ארץ ישראל. The גמרא now asks: there is already a well-known general rule that we follow the lenient opinion outside the land. So רב could simply have said 'like רבי עקיבא, outside the land' and relied on that rule. Why did he need his own case-specific wording?

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say (suggesting better wording)
Like him / according to his view

phrases.english: But let him say: 'The halacha follows Rabbi Akiva
phrases.notes: The גמרא is suggesting a better way for רב to have said it.

phrases.english: outside the Land',
since anyone who is lenient regarding the Land
phrases.notes: Meaning: lenient in a dispute about the laws of the land, such as ערלה

phrases.english: — the halacha follows him outside the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵימָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 27 by offering a simpler wording that would teach the same thing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in Step 27 for why רב used his specific wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known general rule already covers lenient views outside the land, so a short formula would have been enough; רב's long wording seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The general rule might have been limited to tree tithes
steps.stepSummary: Had רב said only that, we might think the lenient rule applies only to מעשר of trees, which is רבנן-level even in the land, but not to ערלה, which is Torah-level in the land. So רב teaches it applies even to ערלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had said that, I would have thought: this only applies to tithing tree fruit, which even in the land itself is only a rabbinic law. But for ערלה, which in the land is a Torah law, I would say we should make a decree even outside the land. So רב teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רב's own wording was needed so we would not wrongly think that ערלה outside the land is forbidden by decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute between רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר was about מעשר on tree fruit, which is only rabbinic even in ארץ ישראל. One might think leniency outside the land is fine for such a weak law, but not for ערלה, which is a Torah prohibition in the land, and so the רבנן might have forbidden it outside the land too. רב's wording makes clear the leniency applies to ערלה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: ערלה is stricter than tree-מעשר because in ארץ ישראל it is a Torah law. Still, רב teaches that outside the land we may follow the lenient view even for ערלה.

phrases.english: If he had said that,
I would have thought: these words apply only
regarding tithes of trees,
which even in the Land itself is only rabbinic;
but regarding orla,
which in the Land is a Torah law,
I might say we should make a decree outside the Land too,
so he teaches us (that we do not).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמַר הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 28 by showing the general formula could have been misread.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הוה אמינא / קא משמע לן: explains why the specific wording was needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general lenient rule might apply only to rabbinic tree-מעשר, and ערלה outside the land would be forbidden by decree because of its Torah status in the land.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even for ערלה, outside ארץ ישראל we follow the lenient view of רבי עקיבא, so the buds may be eaten.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי acts on רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבינא found מר בר רב אשי throwing away the berries and eating the buds of an ערלה caper-bush.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא found מר בר רב אשי throwing away the berries and eating the buds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story of someone acting on רב's ruling. This sets up a challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר רב אשי does exactly what רב said: the berries are ערלה, but the buds may be eaten outside ארץ ישראל. The story shows the ruling being practiced, and it gives רבינא a reason to question why this particular lenient view was chosen.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Ravina found Mar bar Rav Ashi
throwing away the berries
and eating the buds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רב's wording to a practical case of someone following his ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, מר בר רב אשי followed רב: discard the berries, eat the buds.

steps.title: Why not follow בית שמאי, who are even more lenient?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks: if you are following רבי עקיבא because he is lenient, why not follow בית שמאי, who are even more lenient?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is your reasoning? Are you following רבי עקיבא, who is lenient? Then you should act like בית שמאי, who are even more lenient!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges מר בר רב אשי's choice. If the reason is 'follow the lenient view outside the land,' then the most lenient view should be chosen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'follow whoever is lenient outside the land' seems to say: pick the lightest opinion. רבינא claims בית שמאי's view leads to a lighter result than רבי עקיבא's, possibly permitting even the berries. The source for בית שמאי's view is quoted in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your reasoning?
Like Rabbi Akiva, who is lenient?
Then let the master act like Beit Shammai,
who are even more lenient!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי דַעְתָּךְ, כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּמֵיקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבינא responds to what he saw in Step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's practice of following רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If leniency is the reason for choosing an opinion outside the land, the even more lenient view of בית שמאי should be followed.

steps.title: The משנה showing בית שמאי's view on the caper-bush
steps.stepSummary: A משנה: בית שמאי say a caper-bush is כלאים in a vineyard; בית הלל say it is not; both agree it is subject to ערלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A caper-bush: בית שמאי say it is כלאים in a vineyard. בית הלל say it is not כלאים in a vineyard. Both agree it is subject to ערלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings the source for his claim that בית שמאי are more lenient about the caper-bush.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only vegetables, not trees, are forbidden as כלאים in a vineyard. So בית שמאי seem to treat the caper as a vegetable, and a vegetable has no ערלה. This is where the leniency comes from, but the last line, saying both agree it has ערלה, seems to clash with this. The גמרא deals with that next.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Forbidden mixed planting in a vineyard (applies to vegetables and grains)

phrases.english: As we learned: A caper-bush —
Beit Shammai say: it is a forbidden mixture in the vineyard.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הַלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֵין כִּלְאַיִם בַּכֶּרֶם.
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: it is not a forbidden mixture in the vineyard.
Both agree that it is subject to orla.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: צָלָף, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבינא's claim in Step 31.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי hold a more lenient view about the caper-bush than רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כלאים about the caper-bush

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a contradiction: בית שמאי call the caper כלאים, so it is a vegetable, yet both sides agree it has ערלה, so it is a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: This itself is difficult: You said the caper-bush, according to בית שמאי, is כלאים in a vineyard, so it must be a vegetable. Then you taught that both agree it has ערלה, so it must be a tree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses רבינא's argument to fix a problem inside the משנה he quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלאים in a vineyard applies to vegetables, and ערלה applies to trees. A plant cannot be both a vegetable and a tree. Yet בית שמאי seem to apply both laws to the caper.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult (an inner contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a side question about the משנה itself, not a reply to רבינא. רבינא's argument picks up again in Step 35.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: a caper-bush, Beit Shammai say,
is a forbidden mixture in the vineyard,
which shows it is a type of vegetable;
and then it teaches:
both agree that it is subject to orla,
which shows it is a type of tree!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גוּפָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבינא's challenge for a moment to point out a contradiction inside the quoted משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's position in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כלאים implies vegetable and ערלה implies tree, so applying both to one plant is contradictory.

steps.title: בית שמאי are unsure, so they are strict both ways
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי are in doubt whether the caper is a vegetable or a tree, so they are strict both for כלאים and for ערלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: בית שמאי are unsure, so here they act strictly, and here they act strictly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: בית שמאי never decided what the caper is. They just treat it strictly both ways because of the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they do not know whether it is a vegetable or a tree, they apply the vegetable law (כלאים) and the tree law (ערלה) out of caution. So there is no real contradiction. But this means that for them, ערלה here is only a doubt, which becomes important in the next step.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
Beit Shammai are uncertain about it,
and they act here (כלאים) strictly
and here (ערלה) strictly.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inner contradiction raised in Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Doubt explains strictness on both sides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי hold the caper is both a vegetable and a tree, which is contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי are in doubt and are strict in both areas; for them the caper's ערלה status is only a doubt.

steps.title: For בית שמאי the caper is only doubtful ערלה, which is permitted outside the land
steps.stepSummary: Returning to רבינא's challenge: for בית שמאי the caper is ספק ערלה, and a משנה says ספק ערלה is forbidden in ארץ ישראל, permitted in סוריא, and outside the land... (the quote continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, for בית שמאי it is a doubtful ערלה. And we learned: doubtful ערלה is forbidden in ארץ ישראל and permitted in סוריא; and outside the land, one may go down...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבינא's challenge and shows exactly why בית שמאי are more lenient: for them, even the berries are only doubtful ערלה. The quoted משנה is cut off at the end of the amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since בית שמאי are unsure whether the caper is a tree, its ערלה is only a ספק. A משנה rules that ספק ערלה is permitted outside ארץ ישראל. So by בית שמאי, all of the caper, even the berries, could be eaten outside the land, which is more lenient than רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit that may or may not be ערלה
Syria (land conquered by דוד, with an in-between status)
Goes down (into the field), the start of the next line

steps.whyThisMatters: This sharpens רבינא's question: מר בר רב אשי threw away the berries, but בית שמאי's view would allow even the berries outside the land.

phrases.english: In any case,

phrases.aramaic: לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי הָוֵה לֵיהּ סָפֵק עׇרְלָה,
phrases.english: according to Beit Shammai it is a case of doubtful orla,
and we learned: doubtful orla —
in Eretz Yisrael it is forbidden,
and in Syria it is permitted.
And outside the Land, one may go down
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי הָוֵה לֵיהּ סָפֵק עׇרְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 34 (בית שמאי are in doubt) to complete רבינא's challenge from Step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's choice to follow רבי עקיבא rather than בית שמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For בית שמאי the caper is only ספק ערלה, and ספק ערלה is permitted outside the land, so following בית שמאי would permit even the berries.
